answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared escrow before it may trade, with the bond verified across chains through a bridge that checks one hardware-backed identity per agent. The stake makes forging thousands of fake identities expensive, like building a ferrous hull for every ship on a voyage: one honest agent pays once, while a sybil farm must fund a whole fleet. Misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the identity, so attack cost scales with the number of fake agents rather than cheap accounts.
